content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I recently purchased my first [product_name] for a project and I'm having trouble connecting it to my PC. I keep getting a message that the PC and the [product_name] are not on the same subnet. I've changed the subnet mask on the [product_name] from 255.255.255.000 to 255.255.000.000 but can't find a working combination. I've also adjusted the IP address and default gateway to match my LAN IPv4 settings, yet nothing seems to work. When using [product_name] configuration software, I can see the MAC address of the [product_name], so there is some sort of connection, but I'm still stuck. Any help is appreciated.
Could you provide more details? What is the PC's IP address and subnet? What are the IP and subnet for the [product_name]?

LAN (PC) Details: IPv4 Address: 192.168.0.1, IPv4 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0, IPv4 Default Gateway: 192.168.0.2. [product_name] configuration software details: IP Address: 192.168.0.1, Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0, Default Gateway: 192.168.0.2. [product_name] unit: IP Address: 192.168.0.1, Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0, Default Gateway: 192.168.0.2.

Your [product_name] and PC have the same IP address, which causes a conflict. You need to assign a different IP address to the [product_name]. The first three segments should match, but the fourth should be different. Try setting the [product_name] IP to something like 192.168.0.3. Your subnet masks look correct.

I've changed the IP address, but the configuration software still can't communicate with the [product_name]. I receive the same message stating the PC and device are not on the same subnet. Any further suggestions?
Are you connecting directly from PC to [product_name], or are you using a router?
I'm connecting directly from PC to [product_name]. The configuration software detects the [product_name]'s MAC address, so there is some kind of connection.

I've previously created a screen recording showing which settings to select for the PC. If your PC has multiple network interfaces, you need to choose the correct one, as having characters in the interface name can cause issues. When connecting, click the blue double-arrow icon to view available [product_name] units and their settings.

I finally found the right combination of IP, MAC, and default gateway, so now I can communicate with the [product_name]. Thank you for your very helpful video—it gave me ideas on what to check and how to use the software interface in relation to the PC and [product_name] LAN settings.
I'm glad I could assist and that you succeeded. Enjoy working with your [product_name]!

I have the same problem. I can't transfer the program between my computer and the [product_name]. I set the parameters as per your instructions. The program transfer doesn't work, but no error is shown.

Sorry for my previous message; here's the original in English. I experience the same issue: I can't transfer the program between my PC and the [product_name]. The parameters are configured as suggested. However, the program transfer doesn't work and no errors are displayed.

How do you connect your PC to the [product_name]? Is it direct via LAN or through WiFi? Which [product_name] version and firmware are you using? What version of the configuration software do you have?
I connect directly via LAN. Configuration software version is [version_no]. How can I check the firmware version?
I've found something that might help.

I've upgraded to [product_name] configuration software [version_no]. Transferring programs works through LAN, but not via wireless—even after changing the device IP and gateway. I wish I could use both LAN and wireless for transfers.
Wireless connection parameters
Error: Device inaccessible
[product_name] can't use WLAN directly. You need a WLAN adapter with a LAN port or must connect your PC to the [product_name] using LAN.
Yes, it does work with a WLAN adapter. Thank you!
Could you explain this more in detail? I have a WiFi card on my PC—what should I do to get it working? Thanks!
You need a WLAN adapter with a LAN output. Connect that LAN output to the [product_name] using an Ethernet cable. For example, I use a TP-LINK WiFi adapter, model TL-WA890EA.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced issues connecting their PC to a [product_name] using specialized configuration software, mainly related to incorrect IP addresses and subnet masks. Misunderstandings about network settings caused errors about different subnets. Users also struggled to identify correct network interfaces and software menu options. Video guides from other users and forum support were essential for helping newcomers resolve network configuration and software navigation challenges.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a straightforward and well-documented process for connecting their PC to the [product_name], with clear instructions and feedback on proper settings. They seek easier troubleshooting and correction of network setup errors directly through the software or guides.
